notes: The advertised `offset` parameter for `brave_web_search` is defined in the input schema, and `performWebSearch` supports an `offset` argument, but the call handler destructures only `query` and `count` and calls `performWebSearch(query, count)`, so the advertised `offset` is not actually used by the handler. Evidence: dist/index.js:23-27, dist/index.js:107-112, dist/index.js:229-230.

brave_local_search.rationale: `brave_local_search` is advertised unconditionally in `ListTools` and calls fixed Brave Search API endpoints for location lookup, POI details, and descriptions. It returns public local/business data such as `poi.name`, address, phone, hours, rating, price range, and description; if no local IDs are found, it falls back to `performWebSearch`. Public local listings and fallback web results can contain attacker-controllable content, so the output is UNTRUSTED. The tool only contacts fixed Brave API hosts, not an agent-chosen or attacker-readable destination, so it is not a SINK. It does not read local/private user data and does not execute host code.

brave_web_search.rationale: `brave_web_search` is advertised unconditionally in `ListTools` and calls Brave's fixed web search endpoint. It sets the user-supplied `query` as Brave API parameter `q`, fetches from `https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search`, and returns web result `title`, `description`, and `url` as text. Public web search results can include attacker-controlled pages and snippets, so the output is UNTRUSTED. The destination is a fixed Brave API host, not an agent-chosen or attacker-readable destination, so it is not a SINK. It does not read local/private user data and does not execute host code.

value_conditions.default: unset in the environment unless configured by the user/deployment
value_conditions.effect: Required for the server to start. If unset, the process prints an error and exits before serving any tools; when set, both advertised tools are listed unconditionally.
